name: Order Verification Workflow
script_code:
<script>
assignSessionVar("user_email",  source);

whenEvent('render:finish', function () {
  const caseOptionsMap = {
    'Customer Pay': [
      "Item didn't arrive in time",
      "Buyers Remorse",
      "Overage",
      "Rescue",
      "Refused Shipment",
      "Reconsignment",
      "Shipped too soon"
    ],
    'Global Pay': [
      "Wrong Item Ordered",
      "Incorrect Shipping Address",
      "Incorrect Quantity",
      "Missing Item(s)",
      "Missing Assembly Hardware/Parts",
      "Missing Hardware/Parts",
      "Shortage (DS)",
      "Shortage (DC)",
      "Wrong Item Shipped",
      "Item Received Doesn't Match Website",
      "Wrong Account Used",
      "Duplicate Order",
      "Vendor Cost incorrect"
    ],
    'Vendor Pay': [
      "Wrong Item Ordered",
      "Incorrect Shipping Address",
      "Incorrect Quantity",
      "Missing Item(s)",
      "Missing Assembly Hardware/Parts",
      "Missing Hardware/Parts",
      "Shortage (DS)",
      "Shortage (DC)",
      "Wrong Item Shipped",
      "Item Received Doesn't Match Website",
      "Wrong Account Used",
      "Duplicate Order",
      "Vendor Cost incorrect"
    ]
  };

  const subCaseInput = document.querySelector('#subCase');
  if (!subCaseInput) return;

  let allowedSubCases = [];
  let lastParentCase = '';

  setInterval(() => {
    const parentCase = (window.form_data?.parentCase || '').trim();
    if (parentCase && parentCase !== lastParentCase) {
      lastParentCase = parentCase;
      allowedSubCases = caseOptionsMap[parentCase] || [];

      const currentSubCase = subCaseInput.value.trim();
      if (!allowedSubCases.includes(currentSubCase)) {
        subCaseInput.value = '';
        subCaseInput.dispatchEvent(new Event('input'));
        if (window.form_data) {
          window.form_data.subCase = '';
        }
      }
    }
  }, 100);

  subCaseInput.addEventListener('focus', () => {
    const interval = setInterval(() => {
      const menu = document.querySelector('.v-list');
      const items = menu?.querySelectorAll('.v-list-item') || [];

      if (menu && items.length && allowedSubCases.length) {
        items.forEach(item => {
          const label = item.innerText.trim();
          item.style.display = allowedSubCases.includes(label) ? '' : 'none';
        });
        clearInterval(interval);
      }
    }, 100);
  });
});
</script>

67.content:
# claude.md — Order Verification Workflow (GIC / Global Industrial)

## Purpose
Verifies a customer's order, resolves or creates the Salesforce Case for it, adds the
selected order line items to the case, and hands off to the Case Type Routing Tree so
that tree can route the case as a return / cancellation / order edit / etc. Runs inside
the GIC Zendesk/Salesforce agent console.

## Architecture
Seed -> gate (closed case / no session) -> [existing case: fetch + classify] -> one
intake screen -> resolve order key + division -> [known key: exact search] or
[unknown: criteria search] -> grade result count -> select order (if >1) -> resolve
selection -> check for existing cases on this order -> one screen offering
merge / update / new -> case create or merge or update (one script builds the payload,
one Data node per operation, one grading script each) -> wait for GTK key (single
tuned pause, single re-check, no retry loop) -> fetch products already on the case ->
build the line-item queue -> agent reviews/edits quantities on one screen -> loop
(cursor -> add to case -> grade -> more?) with a real agent-click checkpoint every 10
items -> summary -> comments -> hand off to Case Type Routing Tree.

### The line-item loop (the reason for this rebuild)
The previous version (`Order Verification Workflow`, tree 411323165, exported
2026-09-09) advanced this loop with a 1-second `escalate_after` auto-continue on every
pass (baseline nodes 79/80/81/107) — zero agent interaction between line items. An
order with enough line items runs Zingtree's programmatic-jump ceiling out before the
loop finishes ("Workflow execution paused - The last action triggered an invalid
loop"), matching a production issue GIC reported during testing (2026-08-26 Bi-Weekly:
"a production-relevant invalid loop error in order verification... case still creates
despite the error"). The new loop (`cursor_next_line_item` -> `add_case_product` ->
`grade_case_product` -> `route_more_line_items`) is bounded the same way *and* forces
a genuine Content-node click (`screen_checkpoint`, no `escalate_after`) every 10 items,
so the unattended auto-advance streak between real clicks never approaches the ceiling
no matter how large the order is. Batch size is set in `grade_case_product`
(`added_since_checkpoint`) and `route_more_line_items` — change both together.

### Two other auto-advancing loops fixed the same way
The GTK-key wait (baseline nodes 120/121/118: a 3-pass counted retry loop, transforms
`breakloop`) and the products-availability wait (baseline nodes 139/140/149/150/151)
were both the "check -> route back -> check again" anti-pattern the platform's guard
exists to kill. Both are now a single wait node plus a single re-check, no loop-back
edge and no counter. See `references/patterns.md` -> "ONE REQUEST, ONE NODE" in the
zingtree-workflow-builder skill for why a counted retry loop is never the fix.

## Data dictionary
- Inbound (predefined vars, arrive as query params from the launching case/screen):
  `sf_Id`, `sf_OwnerId`, `sf_AccountId`, `sf_Sub_type__c`, `sf_Status`,
  `sf_Approval_Status__c`, `sf_Resolution_Summary__c`, `sf_Description`, `sf_Type`,
  `sf_ContactId`, `sf_Priority`, `sf_Origin`, `sf_Subject`, `sf_Escalation_Reason__c`,
  `sf_Awaiting_Reason__c`, `sf_First_Name__c` — unchanged from the previous version;
  this is the contract the Case Type Routing Tree reads on handoff. Do not rename.
- Native form fields on the intake and search screens are named to match the findorder
  Connected Object's own body template EXACTLY (`orderKey`, `accountKey`, `shipToZip`,
  `billToZip`, `deliveryPO`, `buyerPO`, `GINumber`, `trackingNumber`, `invoiceKey`,
  `rmaKey`, `dateRange`, `case_id`) — camelCase, not house-style snake_case. BUG FOUND
  AND FIXED (2026-09-09, Brent caught it testing the delivered build): an earlier pass
  renamed these to snake_case per house convention, which silently broke the DCO's own
  bare `${accountKey}` / `${shipToZip}` / etc. merges in its request body, since those
  reference the account's already-configured field names, not a scripting convention.
  Native fields that a Connected Object body template reads directly by name are an
  exception to snake_case — they must match the template.
- Form data (session-lifetime, no TTL): `order_key`, `selected_case_id`,
  `division_sf`, `contact_id_sfdc`, `account_id_sfdc`, `has_order_key`,
  `order_count`, `case_count`, `has_products`, `has_contacts`, `has_known_contact`,
  `case_created`, `gtk_key_ready`,
  `line_items_queue` (stringified array — the one structure the loop walks),
  `line_item_index`, `is_more_line_items`, `added_since_checkpoint`,
  `checkpoint_reached`, `line_items_added_count`, `line_items_failed_count`,
  `line_items_table_html`, `insert_comment_text`. `sf_case_type` (set in
  `grade_gtk_key`) is written but not read anywhere inside this tree export — it's
  meant to be read by the Case Type Routing Tree after the handoff (Zingtree carries
  form data forward across an `open_tree` jump in the same session). Unlike the truly
  dead `has_case_order` (removed — `route_intake` already does its own known-order-key
  fallback, making that boolean redundant), this earns a lint warning but isn't dead
  code.
- `transforms.*` (1-hour TTL — used ONLY where a Connected Object's server-side body
  template dot-paths into these exact names; the template itself lives in Zingtree's
  org config and is not visible in this tree export, so these names are preserved
  verbatim from the baseline rather than renamed into form data — see "Import safety"
  below): `orderKey`, `division`, `startDate`, `endDate` (feeding the findorder
  Connected Object, DCO 600 — staged in `route_intake` with a broad 180-day default,
  re-staged in `seed_criteria_search` with the agent's actual date-range/division
  choice; confirmed against the real body template Brent pasted in on 2026-09-09,
  the only one of these six DCOs whose template has actually been verified rather than
  inferred — see the OPEN ITEM below); `accountIdSfdc`, `contactIdSfdc`, `orderIdSfdc`,
  `fName`, `lName`, `email`, `request_reason`, `insertCommentJson` (feeding DCO 609
  case create); `parentSFId`, `parentSFCaseNumber`, `orderIdSfdc`, `accountIdSfdc`,
  `contactIdSfdc`, `Type`, `First_Name__c`, `Last_Name__c`, `Email__c` (feeding DCO 619
  case merge); `sfId`, `insertCommentJson` (feeding DCO 620 case update and,
  separately, DCO 606 add comment); `currentCaseProduct` (a whole dot-pathed object,
  feeding DCO 228 line-item insert).
- `actions.*` aliases (Connected Object ids unchanged from the previous version —
  no Zingtree-side reconfiguration needed for this rebuild):
  226 `get_user_details` (salesforce), 221 `get_case_details` (salesforce, read-only
  usage in this tree despite the id also backing create/update elsewhere in the org),
  756/600 `findordersbycriteria` + PCS pull (http), 223 `get_cases_with_same_order`
  (salesforce, legitimately called from two different order-resolution paths — see
  "Import safety" below), 225 `get_order_products` (salesforce), 608/613 contacts
  (http), 227 `get_account_by_key` (salesforce), 609 case create (http), 619 case
  merge (http), 620 case update (http), 606 case comment (http), 222
  `get_case_order_products` (salesforce), 228 `update_gic_case_product_table`
  (salesforce).
- `views.*`: `findordersbycriteria` (agent's order-grid selection),
  `universal_connector_contacts_by_account` (agent's contact-grid selection),
  `get_cases_with_same_order` (agent's existing-case selection), `get_order_products`
  (agent's selected line items from the product grid).

## External systems
Salesforce (Case, Contact, Account, OrderItem/Order_Product__c objects) and PCS (order
lookup, via HTTP Connected Objects). See the Connected Object list above for exact ids.

## Conventions & gotchas
- `css_include` is GIC's own managed stylesheet
  (`https://assets.zingtree.com/managed/global-industrial/style.css`) — left as-is,
  not the shared `zingtree_2026.css` baseline.
- `show_subtree_persistent_buttons = "1"` is set tree-wide; persistent buttons
  (Escalate etc.) live in a separate Persistent Buttons tree, not on individual nodes
  here.
- Dead code removed in this rebuild: baseline nodes 41 (a `Tree` node whose
  `open_tree_id` was left as `0` — never wired), 90, 101 and 103 (a "Return Freight &
  Sub Case" / "Questions to determine Process Selection" chain, confirmed unreachable
  from the root by the lint tool and a manual graph walk). If this was WIP for a
  feature GIC still wants, it needs to be re-specified as a requirement, not
  resurrected from the dead JSON.
- OPEN ITEM: the Case Type Routing Tree handoff (`goto_case_type_routing`) has
  `open_tree_id = "0"` — same gap as the baseline's node 41. Needs the real tree id
  before this can be imported live.
- OPEN ITEM: whether GIC's Salesforce side can accept a single batched insert of all
  selected line items (e.g. an SObject Collections / Composite API call) instead of
  one Data-node call per item would remove the loop entirely rather than bound it.
  Worth raising with Arun/Vamshi as a follow-up — not attempted here since it requires
  an account-side API decision this rebuild can't make unilaterally.
- One legitimate reuse of the same Connected Object id, documented per house rule
  (`02-data-and-namespaces.md` — mirroring only allowed with a verified consumer on
  each side): DCO 221 (`get_case_details`) is read four times, each a genuinely
  different point in time, not a retry: at session start, again after an existing-case
  fetch, again after case create/update to pick up the just-written type/subtype
  (`fetch_case_type`), and again after a merge to pick up the parent case's type
  (`fetch_case_type_after_merge`).
- BUG FOUND AND FIXED (double API call): DCO 223 (`get_cases_with_same_order`) is now
  called from exactly one node (`fetch_cases_for_order`), reached by both search entry
  points. An earlier pass of this rebuild had copied the baseline's habit of bundling
  223 into the known-order-key search node (`fetch_order_by_key`) too, which — unlike
  in the baseline, where that path never reconverges with the criteria-search path's
  own 223 call — would have made this rebuild call 223 twice back to back for the
  single most common case (an agent typing in an order number that matches exactly
  one order). See `fetch_order_by_key`'s inline comment for the full trace.
- OPEN ITEM / behavior change from the baseline — Case Type Routing handoff coverage:
  tracing the baseline's actual wiring (not just its node labels) found it only ever
  reaches the tree-open node (115, id 1) from ONE of four case-touching end states —
  case-create-found-an-existing-record. The other three baseline end states (explicit
  merge into a selected case: node 92; explicit update of a selected case: node 62;
  and, per a second trace, even a clean brand-new case: node 63) are dead ends with no
  continuation at all — they never reach Case Type Routing. That contradicts the
  stated purpose of this tree (seed a case so Case Type Routing can classify it), and
  reads as exactly the kind of inconsistent wiring "fragile" describes. This rebuild
  deliberately sends every case-touching path (create, merge, update) through
  `goto_case_type_routing`, on the theory that Brent's stated intent is the more
  reliable signal than the baseline's inconsistent wiring — but this is a real
  behavior change, not a faithful port, so please confirm it's what you want before
  any live import, alongside confirming tree id 1 is actually correct.
- Import safety — `transforms` namespace deliberately NOT collapsed into form data:
  the baseline fed DCOs 609/619/620/606/228 with individual named `transforms.*`
  writes (e.g. `transforms.accountIdSfdc`, `transforms.currentCaseProduct` as a whole
  dot-pathed object) rather than a single JSON blob, which strongly implies each
  Connected Object's server-side request-body template is hard-coded to read those
  exact field names. This rebuild preserves those five scripts' `transforms.*` names
  and shapes verbatim (`prep_case_payload`, `prep_case_merge`, `prep_case_update`,
  `prep_case_comment`, `cursor_next_line_item`) even though house style otherwise
  prefers form data — consolidating them into a new shape would silently send an
  empty or malformed payload to Salesforce at runtime, since the template wouldn't
  know how to read it. Every other value in this tree uses form data per house style.
- OPEN ITEM: of the six DCOs this tree stages `transforms.*` fields for, only DCO 600
  (findorder)'s body template has actually been confirmed (Brent pasted it in on
  2026-09-09, which is how the `orderKey`/`division`/`startDate`/`endDate` bug above
  was caught and fixed). The `transforms.*` field names/shapes for the other five
  (609, 619, 620, 606, 228) are still INFERRED from what the baseline's pre-call
  scripts wrote, not confirmed against their actual request-body templates. Given the
  findorder mismatch was real and shipped once already, treat those five the same way:
  don't assume they're right just because they were carried over verbatim. Recommend
  Arun or a Zingtree admin pull/confirm all five before this goes live — and,
  longer-term, that's what would let this handful of fields finally move to form data
  too.
- Flag for review before merge: this tree writes Salesforce Case, Contact and Account
  records (customer PII) — per team policy, have a teammate review the payload-building
  scripts (`prep_case_payload`, `prep_case_merge`, `prep_case_update`) before any live
  import.
